draft.title: Themes that unify a text
card: A theme is a central idea that a text explores, such as loneliness, courage or the cost of ambition. It is more than a topic. It is a point the text makes about that topic.
A theme can hold a text together. Characters, settings, images and events can each add to the same idea, so the parts do not feel separate.

Here is an invented example. In a story about isolation, a boy eats alone, his house sits at the end of a long empty road, and the narrator keeps describing locked doors. Each part feeds the theme of isolation.
To show a theme unifies a text, point to several parts of the text and explain how each one works towards the same idea.
draft.remember: A unifying theme is one central idea that many parts of a text work towards.

a.q: What does it mean to say a theme unifies a text?
opts: Many parts of the text work towards one central idea
The text keeps repeating the same word on every page
Every character in the text feels the same emotion
The text tells one event from several points of view
a.why: A unifying theme links characters, settings and images to one central idea. Repeating a word or sharing an emotion may happen, but neither is what makes a theme hold the text together.
a.clue: Think about how separate parts join up.

b.q: In Priya's short story, a girl moves to a new town. She wears her old school jumper, a grey sky hangs over the streets, and a stray dog is shut out of every yard. Which statement best explains how these parts unify the story?
opts: Each one adds to the idea of not belonging
Each one shows that the town has bad weather
Each one shows the girl dislikes her new school
Each one is a symbol of the girl's old friends
b.why: The jumper, the grey sky and the shut-out dog all suggest being an outsider, so together they build the theme of not belonging. Saying they only show weather or dislike of school treats them as separate details, not parts of one idea.
b.clue: Look for the one idea all three details share.

a.best: Many parts of the text work towards one central idea

b.best: Each one adds to the idea of not belonging

proposal.title: Themes that unify a text
card: A topic is a subject, such as loneliness. A theme is the point a text makes about that topic, such as the idea that loneliness can make people cruel.
A theme can hold a text together. Characters, settings, images and events can each add to the same idea, so the parts do not feel separate.
In an invented story, a boy eats alone, his house sits at the end of a long empty road, and the narrator keeps describing locked doors. Each part feeds one theme: that isolation can trap a person.

b.q: In Priya's short story, a girl moves to a new town. She wears her old school jumper, a grey sky hangs over the streets, and a stray dog is shut out of every yard. Which statement best explains how these parts unify the story?
opts: Each suggests that fitting in somewhere new is hard
Each suggests that the new town has gloomy weather
Each suggests that the girl dislikes her new school
Each suggests the girl will soon forget her old home
b.why: The old jumper, the grey sky and the shut-out dog all suggest being an outsider, so together they build the theme that fitting in somewhere new is hard. Gloomy weather fits only the sky, so it treats one detail on its own instead of linking all three to one idea.
b.clue: Look for the one idea all three details share.
